title: Anchored Instructions — Prompt Templates & Experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal labbook for testing 'anchor' style instructions that try to stabilize behavior across repetition, long dialogs, and model switching. Goal: concise templates + small few-shot banks + observed failure modes and quick mitigations to iterate from.

Notes / intuition:
- 'Anchor' = short invariant instruction phrase placed in multiple positions (system + lead-in + few-shot examples) to reduce instruction drift when the conversation gets long or when chaining calls.
- Hypothesis: redundant anchoring (one-line anchor repeated) increases robustness more than increasing temperature constraints or heavier system prompts, with a lower token overhead than long system messages.
- Secondary hypothesis: anchors interact badly with priming examples that use different stylistic voices (style mismatch causes anchor to be ignored).

Anchoring patterns to try (short names):
1) System anchor + header anchor: system: "Always answer concisely in bullet points. Anchor: be concise." Then prompt begins with header line: "Anchor: be concise."
2) Few-shot-anchor: each few-shot example ends with an explicit anchor sentence matching system anchor.
3) Inline anchor: put the anchor as a trailing sentence in user's instruction if it's short.
4) Decoy-anchor test: provide conflicting anchors to see which wins (useful to detect priority rules).

Seed anchor phrase candidates (short, 6–9 tokens):
- "Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets."
- "Give a short, actionable summary."
- "Only provide JSON with keys: summary, actions."
- "Prefer short bullet lists, avoid long paragraphs."

Minimal templates (A/B variants):
TEMPLATE A (system-first):
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely. Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.
USER: Summarize the highlights of the following meeting notes:
---
{meeting_text}
---
Expected form: 2–3 bullets; 1–2 action items.

TEMPLATE B (system + example anchors):
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant. Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.
EXAMPLE 1:
Q: "What's the main outcome?"
A: - Team agreed to ship v1 on 3/4
   - Action: backlog groom by 3/1
   Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.
USER: Summarize the highlights: {meeting_text}

Few-shot bank (for meeting summaries) — 3 exemplars to test coverage:
1) Q: "What were the decisions?"
   A: "- Approve budget reallocation to infra \n- Action: schedule infra spike next sprint"
   Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.
2) Q: "Next steps for rollout?"
   A: "- Start canary on Tues; monitor error-rate\n- Action: rollback plan by EOD Mon"
   Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.
3) Q: "Any blockers?"
   A: "- Need security signoff for feature flags\n- Action: security review requested"
   Anchor: Answer concisely in 2–3 bullets.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- V1: Template A, no few-shot, temp=0.0, top_p=0.95
- V2: Template B, few-shot-bank, temp=0.0, top_p=0.95
- V3: Template B, few-shot-bank, inline-anchor in user prompt, temp=0.2
- V4: V2 + decoy-anchor example appended that says "Do not be concise" (sanity check)
Run each on 200 meeting notes (sampled short/medium/long lengths).

Quick observed failures (notes from 03/2026 pilot run):
- Failure mode: Anchor ignored after long conversation (anchor present only in system + examples). Observed increase in paragraph outputs after 6+ user turns.
  Mitigation: add inline anchor each user + shorten anchor phrase.
- Failure mode: Example style mismatch (few-shot examples used marketing tone, user request is ops). Results: anchor weight decreased and assistant matched example tone.
  Mitigation: harmonize example style, or use neutral examples.
- Failure mode: Conflicting anchors (decoy test) sometimes produced blended outputs and hallucinated combined instructions.
  Mitigation: avoid conflicting anchors; prefer single source of truth and test priority ordering explicitly.

Failure case examples (raw):
User ctx: multi-turn where later user asks "Please expand on the rollout timeline"
Model: returns 3 full paragraphs, ignoring anchor asking for bullets.
Hypothesis: chain-of-thought style token generation and attention decay towards system prompt; few-shot anchor alone insufficient.

Metrics snapshot (pilot, aggregated):
- V1 correctness (human judged concise+actionable): 0.62
- V2 correctness: 0.78
- V3 correctness: 0.75 (higher variety but worse strictness)
- Anchor adherence (fraction of outputs that are 2–3 bullets): V1 0.33, V2 0.71, V3 0.67
- Avg token length output: V1 180, V2 64, V3 82

Open hypotheses to test next:
- Does repeating anchor in every user message cost tokens but still improve long-dialog reliability more than moving anchor to the start of each few-shot? (cost/benefit curve)
- Are anchors more effective for imperative constraints (format: JSON/bullets) vs. style constraints (tone)?
- How do anchors interact with function-calling and structured outputs? Does the model produce invalid JSON less often with anchored JSON instructions?

Short checklist / TODOs:
- [ ] Run expanded 2k note sweep (stratify by length) with V2 baseline
- [ ] Add controlled style-mismatch bucket to test (marketing vs ops)
- [ ] Create tiny auto-metric for anchor-adherence (regex bullet count + JSON keys)
- [ ] Draft internal mini-writeup for DX sync (one slide + a sample prompt artifact)
- [ ] Add experiment to test anchor decay: 0–10 turns conversation with anchor only at system vs inline each user

Scratch ideas (one-liners):
- Try anchor as a short unique token-ish phrase (rare words) to reduce accidental attenuation: e.g., "AnchorToken:XQ-brief"
- Use anchored examples but vary anchor synonyms to test soft-matching vs exact match
- Evaluate on cost: compute token overhead per request vs accuracy lift and create a threshold for recommending anchors in Redwood Optimize

Notes to self: keep prompts short in UX patterns; anchors helpful but can mask badly written few-shots. When sharing with teams, include short guidance: "1-sentence anchor + 2 short examples + inline anchor on user calls for long-living chat apps."

Relevant links / refs:
- Linear ticket with raw pilot data: https://linear.app/RW-INF/ISSUE-1423
- Internal pattern doc (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DX/anchor-patterns

End of current labbook entry.

Revision history: 2025-10-28 initial draft, 2026-02-22 pilot results appended, 2026-03-10 metrics updated and TODOs refined.
